overview.text: The Brown Tree Snake is a slender, mildly venomous, rear-fanged tree snake from northern Australia, New Guinea and nearby islands. Accidentally taken to Guam, it became a famous invasive species there.

identification.text: Slender, with big eyes with vertical pupils like a cat's. Colour varies: brown, greenish or with bands.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Coastal northern and eastern Australia, eastern Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and other islands of Melanesia.

behaviour.text: Active at night and lives mainly in trees, hunting by sight and smell.

diet.text: Birds, lizards, bats, mice and other rodents; small ones eat frogs and lizards.

recognise.text: Long, thin body with a large head and cat-like eyes.
